change_summary: Back-adjusted 4 unadjusted stock splits in the OHLCV warehouse (KLAC 10:1 <=2026-04-24, CRWD 4:1 <=2026-06-29, DD 1:3 reverse <=2026-06-22, MLI 2:1 <=2026-06-26; 2767 cold + 72 hot rows across both tiers), recorded in new split_adjustments ledger table; added quant/ohlcv_split_repair.py (scan/apply/list CLI, idempotent, crash-resumable) and wired an overlap-day split guard into refresh_warehouse_ohlcv (repair_splits=True default) so future splits are detected and repaired at write time. Strategy behavior unchanged; affected tickers are not in the core traded universe.
changed_variable: warehouse OHLCV split-adjustment consistency (ohlcv_overlay continuity across split boundaries)
hypothesis: Warehouse OHLCV series for tickers that split after their frozen-tier rows were written (KLAC 10:1 at 2026-04-27, CRWD 4:1 at 2026-06-30) carry a permanent unadjusted discontinuity that corrupts returns/ATR/drawdown for any consumer; back-adjust pre-split rows by the round split factor in both tiers and add a write-path split-discontinuity guard to ohlcv_warehouse_refresh.
notes: Vendor-verified split calendar (yfinance): KLAC 10:1 eff 2026-06-12, CRWD 4:1 eff 2026-07-02, DD 1-for-3 eff 2026-06-24, MLI 2:1 eff 2026-07-01. Before scan: 4 cross-batch round-factor discontinuities; after scan: 0; all 4 boundary windows continuous (<30% day moves). Contamination audit: no default-on live/order path consumed corrupt series (core signals price off yfinance directly); contaminated artifacts: data/kova/rs_proxy daily files (KLAC 20260612+, CRWD 20260702+, DD 20260623+, MLI 20260701+; regenerate clean going forward), news_event_exposure_observations rows for KLAC/CRWD after corruption dates; contaminated experiments: exp-20260622-025 (KLAC across boundary), exp-20260702-017 and exp-20260702-018 (KLAC/CRWD theme-peer propagation rows). DD/MLI absent from PEAD broad universe and propagation artifacts. Residual risk: seed_warehouse_from_snapshots(update_existing=True) would regress a repaired ticker only if it appears in snapshot JSONs — none of the 4 do; split_adjustments ledger + scan CLI catch any regression.

parameters.single_causal_variable: warehouse OHLCV split-adjustment consistency (ohlcv_overlay continuity across split boundaries)

post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not reserve further IDs to re-scan or re-apply these four boundaries; the repair is recorded in the split_adjustments ledger and re-runs return already_applied. Do not hand-patch warehouse prices for future splits — the refresh guard handles them; if it misses one, fix the guard, not the data by hand. Routine future guard-triggered repairs are pipeline behavior, not new experiments (fault recovery exemption applies only if the guard itself breaks).
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: A new experiment on this surface needs either a guard false-positive/false-negative on a real future split, a snapshot re-seed regression (repaired ticker appearing in snapshot JSONs), or a non-split adjustment class (e.g. non-round spinoff factors like DD 2.39x on 2025-11-03, which the round-factor scan deliberately does not cover — DD's cold series was single-batch and internally consistent, so no repair was needed there).
post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: Every warehouse write path freezes existing rows (update_existing=False), so a split occurring after a ticker's rows were written leaves stored history at the pre-split scale while later auto-adjusted vendor fetches insert post-split-scale rows next to it. Four such boundaries existed (KLAC/CRWD/DD/MLI). Back-adjusting the stale rows by the vendor-verified round factor restored ohlcv_overlay continuity (scan 4 hits -> 0), and the new overlap-day guard in refresh_warehouse_ohlcv repairs future cases at write time because fetched frames always overlap already-stored dates.

production_impact.note: refresh_warehouse_ohlcv gains a default-on split guard (data hygiene only); no signal/order path changed. Affected tickers are outside the core traded universe; core live signals price off yfinance directly.
